A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELECT research, with matching authors, methods, and principal experiments. All pages, including Appendices A–F, are readable, and relocated or reformatted material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative editing experiments on PIE-Bench and MagicBrush, including seed-selection, prompt-selection, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a human preference study, larger candidate-pool experiments, and further diagnostic analyses in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The core BIS framework and Algorithms 1–2 remain. Appendix C.6 adds an evaluated hybrid selection variant choosing between minimum-background-MSE and maximum-foreground-MSE candidates using a preliminary score. Section 4.3 also corrects the written rectified-flow update increment from t to Δt; an implementation change or rerun is not established.

E1.justification: v2 adds human preference data from 34 participants evaluating 52 selected PIE-Bench cases. Image benchmark and editing-task coverage remain PIE-Bench and MagicBrush; the new global-edit analysis examines PIE-Bench's existing style-transfer task rather than introducing another benchmark.

E2.justification: The five editing models and original Vanilla/Best-of-N/ELECT comparisons are retained. Appendix C.6 and Figure 17 newly compare background-based selection against foreground-MSE selection, CLIPScore selection, and a background/foreground hybrid.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a human-evaluation protocol: 34 participants classify ten seed outputs for each of 52 high-variance, category-balanced cases, with preference aggregated from positive and negative responses. Additional experiments extend candidate pools to N=25, 50, and 100 for IP2P and UltraEdit. The original benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially expands validation through background-MSE ranking analyses and human judgments, larger-pool sensitivity tests, global-style-edit analysis, a concrete under-editing failure, and alternative-score ablations. The earlier timestep and mask-extraction analyses are retained, including the full stopping-step plot relocated to Figure 13.

E5.justification: The new human study reports inter-rater agreement using Krippendorff's alpha=0.7535 and a preference/background-consistency Pearson correlation of r=0.534. These statistical summaries are absent from v1. Repeated-run uncertainty reporting for the retained benchmark results is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 4 retain their numerical values. v2 adds human-preference findings, N=25–100 performance curves, global-edit subset results, and alternative-score comparisons. For example, Appendix C.4 newly reports 26% lower MSE and 3.4-point higher SSIM for IP2P versus fixed-seed evaluation; Figure 17 ranks the hybrid highest across its three models. These are additional comparisons, not improved values for the original experiments.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 changes the rectified-flow denoising update from z_t−v_theta·t to z_t−v_theta·Δt, correcting the mathematical step increment. The BIS definitions, other diffusion/flow equations, and Appendix D are otherwise retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about verifier-free early seed selection, BIS, and MLLM-assisted prompt selection. The headline 41% average/61% maximum computational reduction and approximately 40% recovery of failed cases are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds explanations of global editing through structural coherence, attributes uncommon under-editing to editing models' modification bias, and discusses noisy-latent CLIP failures and excessive foreground changes. It also motivates future multi-objective selection. The original over-preservation limitation and main interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a code-repository link after the abstract, adding explicit code-access information absent from v1. Existing experimental setup descriptions, algorithms, and MLLM prompt templates are largely retained. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning against prior editing and candidate-selection methods remain the same. Appendix A's positioning text moves into Table 2's caption; reference metadata and formatting updates do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the overall section sequence are retained. Changes include localized introduction edits, reversing the Performance/Efficiency discussion order, reorganizing Appendix E, and expanding Appendix C's subsection structure. This is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a two-column layout, places Figure 1 before the abstract, reconfigures the pipeline and qualitative-comparison displays, and relocates the prompt demonstration and full stopping-step plots to the appendix. It also adds the validation, scaling, global-edit, failure-case, and alternative-score figures.

improvement.justification: v1 primarily supports its central background-consistency criterion through automatic metrics. v2 adds direct human validation and competing-score comparisons, substantially strengthening that justification while examining larger candidate pools, global edits, and a concrete failure. These additions improve the evidence for both usefulness and limitations. The selected 52-case study and incompletely specified hybrid score still limit generalization and reproducibility, but the overall evidential gain is substantial.
